articles.title: Xbox Series X Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Xbox Series X launched in November 2020 alongside the Xbox Series S. The flagship Series X is Microsoft's fourth generation in the Xbox console lineup
articles.body:
The Xbox Series X launched in November 2020 alongside the Xbox Series S. The flagship Series X is Microsoft's fourth generation in the Xbox console lineup and features 4K@120fps, ray tracing, a custom 1TB NVMe SSD, and a disc drive. The significantly smaller, digital-only Series S is less powerful, targeting 1440p@120fps, originally offered 512GB of storage , and is ideal for playing Xbox Game Pass.

A 1TB Xbox Series S model launched a few years after the original console, and in 2024, an all-digital 1TB Xbox Series X and 2TB Xbox Series X Special Edition came out. A few other variants have since been released, including the Limited Edition Xbox Series X X25 to celebrate Xbox’s 25th anniversary. Still, no matter the Xbox Series X or Xbox Series S variant, they all perform nearly identically to the originals.

Xbox has confirmed a next-generation console . Project Helix is "designed to be a console capable of playing games from your PC." This project will include a “family of devices” , according to the Xbox CEO Asha Sharma. No other major details have come out, but it could be released as early as late 2027.

Beyond the console, Xbox also offers top handheld gaming PCs that are great for playing Xbox games using Play Anywhere, Game Pass, or Cloud Gaming. The Asus ROG Xbox Ally and the more powerful Asus ROG Xbox Ally X both came out in October 2025. The latest Xbox handheld, the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 , came out in October 2026.

Read this guide to learn more about the Xbox Series X and Series S

IGN tech expert Ryan McCaffrey had the opportunity to conduct thorough hands-on testing of the Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S. Below is what he had to say about each:

“No matter what current games you throw at it, your loading times will be drastically cut, your framerates will be smoother, and your resolutions will be higher. This bold and minimalistically designed box is quiet, compact for both the power it packs and especially how it compares to the PS5, capable, and loaded with convenience features like instantly resuming and cycling between any of your recently played games. Compared directly to the PlayStation 5’s specs, it flat-out gives you more power for the same price. Still, the internal SSD’s space has felt increasingly cramped, making the storage upgrades seem more essential than would be ideal. But Microsoft’s commitment to accessibility, backwards compatibility, and services like Game Pass and Cloud Gaming has paid off – and we’re only beginning to see a future where an Xbox is more than a box.”

“It’s limited to 1440p resolution and has a claustrophobically small storage space, but it’s tiny and quiet, with snappy load times, and can play games at 120 frames per second if your TV can support it. I’m mostly concerned about its long-term viability. Games are only going to get more demanding going forward, so the Series S isn’t something I’d recommend as your main gaming platform. But that doesn’t mean it doesn’t have its place: The Series S is an excellent second console, like if you want something for a kid who plays on a smaller screen or if, for example, you have a PS5 but want to occasionally dip into the smorgasbord that is Game Pass”

The Xbox Series X specs are nearly identical across all of the models, delivering the same overall performance. The only differences are the 2TB model’s storage capacity and the digital-only Series X’s lack of a disc drive, which makes it lighter.

When comparing the Xbox Series S specs to the Xbox Series X, it’s clear the Series S is less powerful based on its processors and RAM. It can only game in 1440p at a max of 120fps, versus the Series X’s 4K support. The Series S has no disc drive and is significantly smaller. However, both of Microsoft’s consoles offer the same connectivity, including storage expansion.

articles.title: GTA 6 Would Probably Run on the Steam Machine
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 isn't coming out on PC right away, but when it inevitably does, it should run on the Steam Machine, albeit at lower settings.
articles.body:
Now that I’ve spent more time with the Steam Machine , I can’t stop myself from looking at Grand Theft Auto 6 looming on the horizon and thinking about how it’d theoretically run on Valve’s new mini gaming PC . Now, of course, it’s going to be a year or two before Rockstar deigns to grace PC gamers with GTA 6, but once it does, it’ll probably be an incredibly demanding PC game.

Since the Steam Machine came out, its performance has been, well, heavily discussed online, to say the least. It’s not hard to see why some folks are skeptical of Valve's little PC – it does cost $1049 to start and is slightly slower than the PS5 most of the time. In spite of that, though, Rockstar’s last couple of PC launches, namely Red Dead Redemption 2 and the Enhanced Edition of Grand Theft Auto V, have been monuments to the scalability of PC games. So the Steam Machine might be more capable of handling everyone’s favorite crime simulator better than you might think.

Now before the Steam Machine even has a chance of running Grand Theft Auto 6, Rockstar actually has to release it on PC. It’s basically inevitable that a PC version will eventually come out, but, according to a Bloomberg interview with Take Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, Rockstar instead wants to focus on its core audience – whatever that means – on consoles before releasing a PC version.

This isn’t new, GTA 5 didn’t come out on PC until 2015, two years after it launched on PS3 and Xbox 360, and Red Dead Redemption 2 had a similar gap. But even in the eight years since Red Dead 2, PC gaming has exploded in popularity to the point where Zelnick himself admitted in that same interview with Bloomberg that PC can make up around 50% of a game’s sales these days.

Maybe Rockstar is just stuck in its ways a bit, but at least with Zelnick recognizing the huge market of PC gamers out there, maybe we won’t have to wait a year and a half for a PC port. Maybe, it’ll just be a year instead. I’ll be keeping my fingers crossed.

Modern Rockstar games have a bit of a weird history with their PC ports. Grand Theft Auto 4 was an absolute nightmare when it came out, but mostly because it required the dreaded Games For Windows Live – which caused performance problems, compatibility issues, and god forbid you ever try to run it on a second machine.

But in the years since, Rockstar’s games have gotten so much better on PC. While I personally find it annoying that Red Dead Redemption 2 doesn’t have any strictly defined graphics presets, that’s really only a problem for testing hardware. Thankfully, for actually tuning the game to run on a wide variety of hardware, Rockstar threw in all kinds of graphics options that make it one of the most scalable games out there right now. Plus, the company embraced the Vulkan engine, which also helps it scale, especially outside of Windows 11.

You can, if you want, make Red Dead Redemption 2 look like absolute garbage. That doesn’t sound appealing right off the bat, but it also means that you can get it to run on pretty much anything. Low Spec Gamer , for instance, was able to get it to run on an 11th-gen Core i3 mobile chip from 2020, albeit at around 20-30 fps. For all the talk about the Steam Machine being underpowered, it’s not that underpowered.

Just a couple days ago, Digital Foundry suggested that, based on the trailers we’ve seen so far for GTA 6, the game will probably run at 30 fps on the base consoles, due to the CPU demand of the open world and Rockstar’s preference to lean more towards quality than performance in its console releases. I don’t think that’s wrong, but once the PC version is out there, Rockstar has a track record of giving gamers a lot of knobs to adjust how the game looks and performs.

Running Red Dead Redemption 2 at 4K with FSR set to Performance, and all the settings mixed between medium, high and ultra, the Steam Machine gets a solid 65 fps. It does look a bit worse than the PS5 version does, but it runs very smoothly on Valve’s PC. Grand Theft Auto 5’s Enhanced Edition also runs really well on the high preset with ray tracing, getting around 60-70 fps depending on where I am.

GTA 6 is going to be more demanding, for sure – just look at the trailer – but I don’t think the Steam Machine’s problem is going to be a graphics problem. The Steam Machine’s problem is probably going to be a SteamOS problem, especially if you want to play GTA Online.

Right now, if you look at Grand Theft Auto 5 on the Steam Deck, the Steam Machine, or really any other PC that’s running Linux, you’ll see a big ol’ banner telling you that it’s unsupported. That’s a bit misleading, the game will absolutely run on SteamOS, but only if you want to play the story mode.

GTA Online, which is certainly not going anywhere once GTA 6 launches, uses BattlEye Anti-Cheat, and that doesn’t play well with SteamOS because it needs kernel access. Now, Rockstar could, with its vast resources, probably get a workaround that runs on Linux. But, remember, this is the same company that says its core audience is console gamers. Even when the PC version inevitably comes out, I just don’t see Rockstar paying much mind to SteamOS compatibility issues.

Because no matter how great gaming on Linux has grown over the last few years, it’s still a very small segment of PC gamers. According to the latest Steam Hardware Survey , Linux makes up for just 3.9% of Steam’s install base. That’s admittedly more than macOS, but I don’t think it’ll be enough to convince Rockstar to change its Anti-Cheat service of choice.

There will come a time when GTA 6 runs on the Steam Machine – I don’t think there’s really a question of whether or not the game will work. However, Valve’s little PC will probably only be able to run the single-player campaign, and at graphics settings that might make it look a bit worse than its console counterparts.

Jackie Thomas is the Hardware and Buying Guides Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: How to Get a Decoder and Raid Other Players - Rob Run Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Decoders are a rare item that you can acquire while playing Rob Run. They're tricky to find, though, and very valuable, as they're used to raid other
articles.body:
Decoders are a rare item that you can acquire while playing Rob Run . They're tricky to find, though, and very valuable, as they're used to raid other player's houses . It's a good way to make a lot of money as players leave a majority of their items and money at these locations. In this guide, we'll cover everything you need to know about where to get a Decoder and how you use it to raid other players while playing Rob Run.

The best way to get Decoders is by seeking them out in Looty Bay. There's a chance they can appear as a random drop from looting any shop or house that you can break into through this area. Unfortunately, they do not have a set drop location, which can make them tricky to locate.

When you do find one, bring it with you out of Looty Bay and take it back to your house. If you have suitable defenses, leaving them in your home's storage is the best place until you're ready to begin raiding other players.

If you're looking to get purple Decoders , the Epic rarity, you can head to the Suspicious Door at Lenny's Motel and exchange three Decoders and $10,000 for one, or a full epic Action Camera.

When you're ready to raid other players, head to any of their homes within the various available Settlements . However, you need to double-check the type of Decoders you've looted. You'll be able to see it when hovering over the item. Each rarity of Decoder allows you to invade a higher-quality base. Green Decoders take down one level of a player's defenses, while the purple Decoders (the Epic Decoders) allow you to take down three levels. You can interact with a player's Security System on their fences and on the front section of their bases to begin using them.

Not only do you want to double-check that you have the correct Decoders, but you need multiple of them. Each security stage at a player's home requires you to use a Decoder, and the more Fuses a player has on their base's defenses, the more Decoders you need.

Players begin with level five defenses, but expect players with a lot of items inside their homes to have multiple fuses. The more you have, the more security defenses you can break through to reach the house. You can then head to any of the available Settlements with houses, and drive around until you find a home that you want to raid.

Higher-level Settlements will have more defenses, and you will absolutely need more than three Decoders to break through. You can interact with the security boxes at the front of these homes when you're ready to break in. If there's a security module installed in the home, the player (and other clan members associated with that player) may receive a notification if they're online. You'll then only have a short amount of time to grab everything and escape.

articles.title: All Big Poe Locations - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: One of the major changes from the original Ocarina of Time lies in how Big Poes are tracked down to get the final Empty Bottle (which, in the Remake, is the
articles.body:
One of the major changes from the original Ocarina of Time lies in how Big Poes are tracked down to get the final Empty Bottle (which, in the Remake, is the fifth Bottle and in the original was the fourth). The other change is that the Big Poes now inhabit haunted objects, highlighted by an eerie purple glow and a Poe lantern on a stick next to it.

Requirements: Adult Link, Epona, Fairy Bow, Empty Bottles

The Big Poes side quest is one only accessible to Adult Link. To complete it and get the Bottle, you’ll have to find and catch 10 Big Poes across Hyrule Field, and bring them to the Poe Collector in the Ghost Shop in the remains of Hyrule Castle Town.

To start the quest, find the Poe Collector in Hyrule Castle Town, who is waiting in the first door to the right after entering the area as Adult Link. It's the same room with the bored soldier and all the pots you can break as Young Link. Ask the Poe Collector about points and he will reveal that he’ll give you something for catching Ooes if you earn 500 points. You earn 100 points per Big Poe brought to him.

Golden Rupee (200) and Adult's Wallet: Deliver 10 Poes

To capture a Big Poe, you have to first find and activate them, then chase them on horseback and hit them with two arrows. The collectible soul (yellow color) they leave behind can be captured with an Empty Bottle, so make sure you've got empty ones when you set out or you'll have to run back and forth.

Here are the locations and checklists for all 10 Big Poes found in Hyrule Field in Adult Link's quest line.

The first Big Poe can be captured in the north of Hyrule Field, just east of the entrance to Hyrule Castle Town.

Look for a haunted rock glowing purple. Jump over it with Epona to flush out the Poe and start the hunt. Capture the soul.

The second Big Poe is found to the south of the drawbridge leading into Castle Town, alongside the stone path.

Look for a broken wall element, highlighted by the Poe's signature purple lamp. Leap over it and complete the hunt.

The third Big Poe is located in the grove near the entrance to Lon Lon Ranch.

Look for a wooden fence element sitting at the side of the dirt path leading to the ranch. Leap over it with Epona to face the Poe.

The fourth Big Poe is located not far away from the last one. Go to the west side of the northern part of Lon Lon Ranch.

You'll find a felled tree in the middle of the meadow just outside of the Lon Lon Ranch fence. Jump over the log and chase the Big Poe for another bottled trade item.

Big Power number 5 is found in western Hyrule Field. You'll know you're in the right place once the green meadows make way too a barren steppe landscape.

Spot a haunted rock near the entrance to Gerudo Valley. Activate the Poe and capture it.

The sixth Big Poe is located not too far from the spawn point of the last one. From the barren area near the Gerudo entrance, follow up the hill slopes to spot another fallen tree near where the rock splits the landscape.

Get a running start on Epona and leap over the log to get the hunt started, then bring the Big Poe to the quest-giver.

The seventh Big Poe is located in the very south of Hyrule Field, in the wooded area near the path to Lake Hylia.

You'll find the haunted object, another fallen tree, in the midst of the forest area. Check that you have an Empty Bottle and chase down the Poe.

Big Poe number eight is located in the southeast portion of the Hyrule Fields, in the marshlad area.

Spot another fallen tree in the middle of the meadow to the south of the waterlogged area nearby. Have Epona leap over the log and chase down the Big Poe.

The ninth Big Poe is located on the east to southeast side of Hyrule Field, just before the path back into Link's childhood home of Kokiri Forest.

You'll see a rotten tree on the slop leading up to the forest path. Leap over it with Epona and collect the penultimate Big Poe.

The tenth and final Big Poe is located towards the center of Hyrule Field's map. Ride to the east side of Lon Lon Ranch's horse corral and you'll easily spot the purple glow of the last haunted object.

This one's another broken wall, perhaps belonging to a farmstead ruin or old barn from bygone days. Saddle up, jump over the obstacle, chase and shoot the Big Poe, and you can deliver the bottled goods to unlock your final reward.

Now that you've collect all 10 Poes, head back to Hyrule Castle Town, enter the storage building to the right, and deliver the last souls to the Poe Collector. You will receive not one, but two rewards for completing the quest!

First, Link will get a Gold Rupee, worth 200.

This completes the Big Poe quest. You can still chase and sell regular Poes for Rupees, of course.

articles.title: Gun Durability - Rob Run Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Your guns and weaponry gradually break down as you use them in Rob Run. It's a way to ensure you're consistently spending money and have something to
articles.body:
Your guns and weaponry gradually break down as you use them in Rob Run . It's a way to ensure you're consistently spending money and have something to use as you continue to finance your criminal activities. As it stands, Rob Run is in early access, and gun repairs are not available in the current build. However, the development team has promised that they're on the way. Here's what we know about gun durability in Rob Run.

In a Steam news post released on Nov. 13, the team addressed some of the community's most frequently asked questions and mentioned that gear durability degrading is a deliberate choice to help balance the in-game economy.

However, weapon and gear repair will be available in a future update .

A weapon's durability decreases every time you die. All weapons have the same durability threshold, regardless of their rarity or quality, which is three . Once it reaches zero, the weapon is broken and won't fire. You can inspect a gun's durability by highlighting it while it's in your inventory. It will be under the weapon's magazine size and weapon range graph.

For now, though, any weapon that loses durability cannot be repaired in Rob Run. If there's a weapon you want to continue using, store it somewhere in your home, and wait for the weapon repair kits to become available. We'll also be updating this section when we learn more about how this gameplay mechanic works for everyone.

articles.title: How to Make the Sweet Apple Pie Habitat - Pokemon Pokopia Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Applin and Appletun are two Pokemon joining us in Pokopia thanks to the Apples to Applin Event that runs from November 16th to December 1st, but their Habitat
articles.body:
Applin and Appletun are two Pokemon joining us in Pokopia thanks to the Apples to Applin Event that runs from November 16th to December 1st , but their Habitat isn't going to make itself! If you're wondering how to build the Sweet Apple Pie Habitat to entice Applin and Appletun into your town, you'll find everything you need in this Pokemon Pokopia guide.

The Sweet Apple Pie Habitat that entices Applin and Appletun can be created using 1x Apple Pie , 1x Seat , and 1x Table . The Apple Pie can be purchased from the Pokemon Center using 10x Syrupy Apples, and you can use any old table and chair to make up the rest! Once you've got your items, place the table put the Apple Pie on top, and set up a chair to create the Sweet Apple Pie Habitat.

Syrupy Apples are a unique event-related fruit that only grows on Dream Islands. You won't find any of these sweet snacks in any of the regular Pokemon Pokopia regions at the start of the event, so you will have to set off to a Dream Island to find some.

Once you reach the shores of your Dream Island, start wandering around and search for trees with apples growing on them. The trees themselves look just like Leppa Berry Trees, and the apples are red on top and orange on the bottom. Once you find one, headbutt the tree to collect two Syrupy Apples.

You can get two Syrupy Apples per tree, and the items at Applin's store are pretty pricey. If you want to unlock all items required to build the three habitats that are part of this event, you will need 65-70 Syrupy Apples. Collect every Syrupy Apple on your Dream Island to make sure you have enough!

The Apple Kitchen Habitat that houses Applin and Flapple is the toughest and most expensive Habitat to create in the Apples to Applin event. To get started, you'll need a whopping 45x Syrupy Apples to purchase the Appley Blender, Dipplin Mixing Bowl, and the Kitchen Scale .

Then, you need to track down 3x Kitchen Tables . No other table will do, so if you don't have the Kitchen Table recipe unlocked, you might be in trouble! Luckily, we know where you can find one in the wild, so you don't need to stress about having to find the recipe organically in glowing water ripples.

There is one Kitchen Table sitting in one of the buildings behind the Pokemon Center in Bleak Beach. To find it, head over there and stand facing toward the Pokemon Center. Head down the road on the left side of the Pokemon Center and follow it until you reach the last house by the water. There is a pretty well stocked kitchen in there, including a Kitchen Table! Take a picture of it using Item Mode on your camera so you can 3D Print two more, and snatch that one up to finish your habitat.

It costs 10x Pokemetal Ingot to 3D Print 1x Kitchen Table, so you will need 20x Pokemetal Ingots in total. Once you've got all your materials sorted, place all three Kitchen Tables next to each other, place the Appley Blender on the first one, the Dipplin Mixing Bowl in the middle, and the Kitchen Scale on the right to create the Apple Kitchen Habitat.

Syrupy Apples are a unique event-related fruit that only grows on Dream Islands. You won't find any of these sweet snacks in any of the regular Pokemon Pokopia regions at the start of the event, so you will have to set off to a Dream Island to find some.

Once you reach the shores of your Dream Island, start wandering around and search for trees with apples growing on them. The trees themselves look just like Leppa Berry Trees, and the apples are red on top and orange on the bottom. Once you find one, headbutt the tree to collect two Syrupy Apples.

You can get two Syrupy Apples per tree, and the items at Applin's store are pretty pricey. If you want to unlock all items required to build the three habitats that are part of this event, you will need 65-70 Syrupy Apples. Collect every Syrupy Apple on your Dream Island to make sure you have enough!

articles.title: GTA 6: How one school is battling the 'GTA flu' with warnings to parents and prizes for pupils
articles.summary: Belfast Boys' Model school issued letters to parents, saying that the release of the game on Thursday coincided with GCSE maths exams.
articles.body:
A school concerned about pupils not coming in on the day the highly-anticipated GTA VI video game is released has offered young people prizes for turning up for classes.

Belfast Boys' Model school issued letters to parents, saying that the release of the game on Thursday coincided with GCSE maths exams.

The school said that "activities such as playing Grand Theft Auto can wait until the weekend".

On Monday, the school added that pupils who attended school on both Thursday and Friday would be entered into a draw for a £70 gift card for either PlayStation or Xbox.

In a letter issued to parents, reported by The Nolan Show , the school reminded "all parents and carers of the importance of ensuring that students attend school on Thursday 19th November".

It also said that "all Year 11 students and some Year 12 students" would be sitting a GCSE maths exam on Thursday, the same day the game comes out.

"Good attendance is one of the strongest indicators of academic success," the letter added.

Mary Montgomery, who is principal of the school, said "the primary focus" of her letter was Thursday's Mathematics examination and "encouraging our boys to be in school and ready to achieve their best".

"The results at GCSE have been fantastic in recent years and we want to continue that success for the boys," she said.

"It also highlighted the launch of GTA as something which might entice some boys to stay at home. However, the games vouchers were a pupil-led incentive."

GTA VI is released on Thursday, 13 years after the previous edition and with an estimated development cost of more $1bn (£866m).

In 2013, the term 'GTA Flu' was coined in reference to the large number of sick days reportedly taken when GTA V was released.

On Monday, the school announced that all pupils in attendance on Thursday and Friday would be entered into a draw to win one of two £70 gift cards "for PlayStation/Xbox".

Anthony, a 15-year-old pupil at the school told BBC News NI he is "very excited" about the game.

He has already downloaded it and when it is released he is "going to play it a lot".

"I've been waiting a long time for this," he said.

"You can pre download it now, install it now and when the game comes out you can instantly play it."

Michael, who is 17, is also excited to play the new GTA game, adding he thinks the school's idea to incentivise attendance is a "really good one".

The idea for the draw, which came from the pupils, will mark International Men's Health Day and raise money for charity.

"This idea is a really good one because gaming and mental health coincide a lot with men as they can use gaming as escapism from personal problems such as school, work and exams," Michael said.

He added: "We think gaming can be used as a way to negate the problems and stress that arise from school, so we brought that idea for the vouchers to get more people into school."

He added that gaming can help the pupils "switch off and manage some of the stress around exams, which is important with GCSE modules this week".

Speaking to The Nolan Show, a former school principal Kathleen O'Hare said the decision to send the letter to parents was "very wise".

"The cult of this game is so large that parents will be put under extreme pressure at times," she said.

O'Hare added that it has been "proven" that missing a day of school "really does matter".

Pete Wray, a Ulster Unionist Party councillor who works with children, said "there is a sizable amount of young people that are in our education system and completely disengage".

"They take an odd day off, and once they've got one day off, they're anxious about going back because they know they're going to be behind, and that leads to more and more problems," he said.

Wray said he will be imploring young people not to miss school to play the game, but that he "completely understands how people can become engrossed in it".

Considered one of the most highly-anticipated video games in history, the game is the latest in the long-running Grand Theft Auto series.

The game series, which has attracted controversy in the past over its depiction of violence and crime, is also the most expensive game ever made, with estimates putting development costs at more than $1bn (£866m).

The previous game in the series, GTA 5, sold nearly 230 million copies, making it one of the best-selling games of all time, which has generated billions of dollars in revenue for developer Rockstar.

GTA 6 will feature its first ever playable female protagonist in a 3D setting - Lucia - alongside her partner in life and crime, Jason, as a second playable character.

Like other GTA games before it, the sixth chapter is set in a fictional US state - this time in Leonida, which is Rockstar's version of Florida.

articles.title: Warnings, Encouragement, and Gift Cards: How Schools Are Preparing for Mass Absences on GTA 6 Launch Day
articles.summary: As GTA 6 launch day nears, schools are preparing for mass absences among pupils by issuing warnings to parents — and offering children the chance to win gift cards just for turning up.
articles.body:
As GTA 6 launch day nears, schools are preparing for mass absences among pupils by issuing warnings to parents — and offering children the chance to win gift cards just for turning up.

While GTA 6 is an 18+ game, an array of U.K. schools are now preparing for kids to skip classes later in order to play Rockstar Games' hugely anticipated new release when it arrives this week.

Numerous schools have warned parents about letting their child stay home this Thursday and Friday — and indeed about playing the 18+ game altogether. Somewhat amusing, several of these warnings do not name GTA 6 specifically, but simply refer to it as a "highly anticipated game" or similar.

"Staff are aware of childing [sic] discussing it and that some have suggested being 'absent' on that day," reads a note shared on social media . "Naturally we are concerned about any such discussions. Please be aware and vigilant of this should you have a child who is a keen gamer."

Another note seen by IGN also referred to a "highly anticipated game" and stated that "playing a computer game is clearly not a valid reason to be absent from school as I am sure you will agree."

But not everyone is taking the same approach. In Spain, one teacher's note has gone viral on X/Twitter after they stated this week would be free of homework so pupils could play uninterrupted. "When GTA 5 came out in 2013, I was your age," the teacher noted sympathetically, stating that they had also delayed an upcoming exam from November 23 to November 30 as well.

And in Ireland, a Belfast school has told pupils and parents that "activities such as playing Grand Theft Auto can wait until the weekend," with kids who do show up this Thursday and Friday automatically entered into a prize draw for a £70 ($90) gift card for PlayStation or Xbox — enough to buy the game themselves (or get a parent to do it).

"The results at GCSE have been fantastic in recent years and we want to continue that success for the boys," Mary Montgomery, principal of the school, told BBC News . "It also highlighted the launch of GTA as something which might entice some boys to stay at home. However, the games vouchers were a pupil-led incentive."

Yesterday, senior U.K. politician Kemi Badenoch, leader of the Conservative Party, said she was less worried about the content of GTA 6 than the idea that kids would spend too long locked away in their bedrooms playing it . "I would be more worried about the amount of time people were spending on a game than the game specifically," Badenoch said. "I remember in my childhood playing Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter — I didn't hit anybody after playing those games."

GTA 6 is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time, and some companies have even given staff bonus time off to play it . We've got plenty more on GTA 6 ahead of its November 19 launch, including details on the New Zealand trick people are using to play early, Gangland Tales From the Frontline of Rockstar's Real-Life Grand Theft Auto Research , and How Gaming's Top Content Creators Are Preparing for GTA 6's Launch and Beyond .

articles.title: In the Wake of Jensen Huang Scandal, Nvidia Establishes National Security and Export Control Committee
articles.summary: Last week, Nvidia CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down amid a scandal involving multiple affairs and alleged suspected espionage. In the aftermath, Nvidia has created a new oversight committee to make sure the company is complying with trade laws.
articles.body:
Last week, Nvidia CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down amid a scandal involving multiple affairs and alleged suspected espionage. In the aftermath, Nvidia has created a new oversight committee to make sure the company is complying with trade laws.

In order to tighten up the company's weak points in the face of a scandal that may have involved $12 billion in AI chips being funneled into China, according to The Times , the Nvidia Board of Directors today implemented a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee. This new committee will be let the board have oversight into the company's national security policies and export control compliance.

According to Harvey Jones, chairman of Nvidia's Board, "Nvidia recognizes that advanced silicon technologies and the emergence of artificial and superintelligence present unprecedented challenges for national security. As the world’s leading advanced computing company, Nvidia has both a responsibility and an opportunity to lead the industry in addressing these challenges. We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation."

This new committee is springing up right after speculation appeared over the weekend that former CEO Jensen Huang was trying to return to the company . Though, subsequently, the board rejected that it was even considering Huang's return , and now that this committee has been established, it looks even more unlikely.

Initially, when Nvidia first announced its investigation into Huang, it didn't look like there were any company secrets that were compromised. Whether or not new information has changed that initial statement is unknown, but this new committee should act as a safeguard to prevent future security breaches.

Meanwhile, the U.S. has confirmed an investigation into Megaspeed, which is suspected of violating U.S. export controls by helping to ship Nvidia's chips to China. According to the BBC , the U.S. Department of Justice and Department of Commerce said they had been investigating the Singapore-based firm Megaspeed since 2024. Huang is alleged to have had an affair with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. China has denied allegations of spying.

Last week, Huang received support from Nvidia employees who called for his return. The former Nvidia boss also won support from other tech CEOs, such as Elon Musk and Epic Games boss Tim Sweeney.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: GTA 5 Fans Make One Last Emotional Ride Through Los Santos Before Heading to Vice City
articles.summary: Ahead of GTA 6's release, GTA 5 fans are reflecting on their 13 years of history with the beloved open-world crime game.
articles.body:
Today, gamers around the world are saying their goodbyes to GTA 5 , a game that has been with them for as long as 13 years. Its initial release was a massive moment for many; not only was it yet another exciting new, ambitious entry into one of gaming’s most beloved franchises, but it would also be a catalyst for so much more for millions of people.

For me, I was just 12 years old. It was an inappropriate age to be playing such a game, but after following the pre-release hype for months and playing it myself, it had a massive impact on me. It set me on the path that I am on today and inspired me to pursue a career in games media, partially so I could cover GTA 6 when it came out.

And now, we’re here. I have spent literally half of my life chasing this moment. It was a journey of all kinds of ups and downs, but I am hardly alone in that journey. Millions of GTA 5 fans have forged friendships, lost loved ones, and experienced life-altering changes during the game's undeterred longevity.

Take GTA YouTuber TGG as an example . He has 2.32 million subscribers, and his story largely traces back to GTA 5. Although he had dabbled in other GTA games prior to this, 5 was the game that really hooked him. In 9th grade, his dad bought him the game and essentially unlocked a whole new world for him. The sandbox elements within GTA Online were immediately captivating for a young teenager, leading to memories he still holds dearly to this day.

“It was freedom,” he said in reference to what made GTA Online special in its earliest days. “No other game would just drop people in an open world and say, 'Do whatever the f**k you want.'"

But it wasn’t just about blowing stuff up or mowing down NPCs for him. When things weren’t going well at home or in his personal life, GTA Online offered an escape, but one that wasn’t overly-isolating. It was like a virtual third space where he could hang out with people from school and find common ground, allowing him to make new friends with kids he may not have otherwise been able to connect with.

“I think one of the reasons those memories are so special to me was because it helped [me make friends]. Racing with people from school, you end up with a full lobby of 16 people. Maybe you only know three or four of them very well, but that's 10 new people from your school that you're racing with that you can build friendships with. And being able to talk about whatever happened in a race or whatever happened in a mission that you were grinding out together, and having an icebreaker with people at school the next day really helped. I don't want to say [it] helped [me] get through school necessarily, but [it] helped expand my circle.

"And to me, as someone who was always a more quiet kid and wasn't the most popular kid in school, those [moments] were very important to me. And I think looking at it a bit deeper, that's probably the reason that those memories are more special to me because they helped me expand my circle at school when it was probably pretty small.”

TGG eventually spun his love and encyclopedic knowledge of GTA Online into a career. He launched a YouTube channel while he was still in school and took inspiration from another creator known as TmarTn for the kinds of videos he wanted to make. After making over a thousand videos, TGG has become a leading source for GTA news, partially because he is the one breaking it himself. He was invited to Rockstar North earlier this year and given the opportunity to preview the game, allowing him to bring a bunch of exclusive info back to his viewers. It’s a surreal moment.

TmarTn, whose real name is Trevor Martin, is still making GTA videos. He has over 5.69 million subscribers on his most active channel and has made countless videos about the franchise. GTA 6’s launch is a sort of full circle moment for him, as his journey with the franchise largely began with the original Vice City.

“The first one I had was Vice City on PS2. So it's kind of cool because it's this full moment. I was a little kid playing this, worried about the loading screens that were popping up and things like that, trying to hide it from my mom. And now I'm back in Vice City and I'm a grown mid-thirties man and I'm still... It's kind of the same vibe. You know what I mean? It's still just as exciting.”

TGG and TmarTn aren’t the only ones whose love for GTA 5 led to fruitful careers. 31-year-old Adam Butterworth was a fan of the game since day one and it became a staple of his life. Every December, Rockstar adds snow to GTA Online and a bunch of holiday festivities, and experiencing this became a holiday tradition for Butterworth.

“Every Christmas Day me and a few mates would load the game [up], [drive] to the parking lot in the city center, go to the roof, and just chat while trying to push each other off the roof or break the car. It was stupid but it was a good time and as we got older and game time became harder to get among us it became something we would be excited for on Christmas… besides the ungodly amount of food and presents.”

Eventually, his love for GTA 5 turned into something more: a job at Rockstar Games. After bearing the elements in a historic UK snowstorm to attend a job interview, Butterworth scored a gig working in the developer’s QA department. In the lead-up to his first day at the company, he immersed himself even further into GTA 5’s world.

“While waiting for my start date, every day I would do the drive around the map and just think that in a few weeks I would get to work with the team that made this game, a game that meant so much to me.”

A Rockstar community member named Josh, AKA Vinewood Motors, has also managed to turn GTA Online into something more than just a game. After building a sizable social media presence sharing content, Josh began to use his following for good. He has raised over $40,000 for charity as part of a series of GTA-centric Gameblast streams over the years. The annual charity streams have become so significant that Rockstar Games has also supported them.

Still, some people don’t have grand ambitions for GTA Online. Some of them just want somewhere they can spend their time and be social. A 22-year-old GTA 5 fan named Harry told me that he spent over 4,300 hours in the game over the last decade. Not unlike others, it has become a source of core memories with his friends.

“Over the last 11 years, I’ve had so many fond memories doing heists, races, adversary modes, and just running around in freemode. I still remember the rush my friends and I felt after finally completing the Doomsday Heist finale for the first time, after many attempts and a lot of arguing.”

All of those memories have culminated in a special event that players are dubbing “The Last Ride.” This isn’t an official in-game event from Rockstar, it’s one created by the community. Players will drive around San Andreas by looping around its highway before ending up at the airport. They then plan to board a jet and fly off into the east toward Vice City while the sun sets behind them. It’s a way to say goodbye to a place they’ve called home for years.

“My plan for GTA 6 launch night is to drive around Los Santos with my friends and talk about some of our favourite memories,” said Harry. “We’re gonna take our favourite cars, say goodbye to landmarks like the casino, our yachts, apartments, and nightclubs. Then, as soon as the clock strikes midnight, we’re opening GTA 6.”

“I’ll say goodbye to a game that has seen me go from university, to Rockstar, to Remedy [Entertainment], to being a home owner, getting married and becoming a dad,” said Butterworth. “13 years of enjoyment and memories.”

Like many others I spoke to for this story, 22-year-old Brian Berkman got GTA fever at a young age and had to wear down his mom so she’d buy the game for him. Now, as he prepares to leave GTA 5 behind, he’s driving through Los Santos like he’s leaving his hometown behind.

“It sounds a little corny on paper but this is the one singular video game that has stuck around for what feels like my entire life; some people have that with Minecraft but I was admittedly never as big a Minecraft guy as others,” said Berkman. “It’s always been GTA 5 for me even before I owned the game myself, sometimes it feels like I know the in-game map better than my own real-life neighborhood sometimes.

“Even when I’d have nothing to do in the game itself I’d find myself driving around Los Santos blasting Non-Stop-Pop FM feeling like I had my own home away from home, while simultaneously in the comfort of my own home. Everytime I’d think this game was getting too old, Mike Posner 'Cooler Than Me' would come on and all of that would wash away, and I’d feel like I was playing the coolest game in the world. Hearing that come on the radio one last time will have me unreasonably emotional on November 18.”

This will also be a moment for some fans to honor those who didn’t make it to GTA 6. 28-year-old Tobias Johnson plans to use this send off to GTA Online as a way to remember his friend, Noah, who passed away almost a decade ago.

“[This] will be a chance to relive the memories I was able to have with my friends, especially Noah, who I lost at 19 years old in 2017,” said Johnson. “I think about him every day and some of the best memories I have of him are from playing whatever random game mode or race on GTA Online together. The last ride will be symbolic for me as this is kinda just taking that next step in life.

“I’m almost 30 now and while I can always go back to GTA 5, this will be a nice little bit of closure on that time of my life and it will be incredibly cathartic to drive around Los Santos and really soak in those memories of Noah and I one last time.”

While some people will write all of this off as “just a game,” it can’t be stressed enough that it’s not really about that. GTA 5 has been sort of a companion for the last decade and a half. It’s about people having one constant thing during a long period in their lives where they experienced a lot of change. It was something they could routinely come back to because GTA Online is more accessible for casual play than some other games. You can fire up the game one evening and never fire a gun or commit a major felony.

Sometimes, all you want to do is cruise around in a flashy sports car while a radio station that feels like it’s frozen in the early 2010s scores your drive. Maybe you want to go hang out at the casino and gamble fake money away. It’s something you can do by yourself, or with a group of friends. It’s a place where your mind can be free. There’s no skill-based matchmaking to ruin your adrenaline rush. There’s no timer or score limit that brings an end to your fun. As TGG said, it’s freedom to do whatever the f**k you want.

GTA 5 has followed me through half my life. From 7th grade to writing for IGN at 26 years old, this game has been there every step of the way. Every crush, every girlfriend, every break up, every pet, every major life decision. I graduated school, got laid off, made stupid choices, and learned from those stupid choices. GTA 5 was there every time I needed a late night drive or something to blow up. It was there when my friends and I had nothing to play, but wanted to do something passive so we could talk.

Final drive complete. Goodbye Los Santos. We're headed to Vice City. — TGG (@TGGonYT) November 16, 2026

Final drive complete. Goodbye Los Santos. We're headed to Vice City.

As some fans step on to these virtual planes to head to Vice City, they’re not just headed to a new game. They’re embarking on a new chapter of their life. New relationships will be discovered, old ones will be strengthened. Would-be creatives will be inspired to create. Maybe it’s also a chance to feel like a kid again. It’s an opportunity to go back to that time where everything was right in their world, when things were simple and there was a way to escape in a different world. In the unruly chaos of a GTA game, people have found peace and catharsis… and there’s nothing wrong with hoping GTA 6 can restore or even build upon that feeling even more.

articles.title: Macaulay Culkin Returns as Kevin for the McDonald's Home Alone Meal, Featuring Collectible Socks and a New Pizza Sauce
articles.summary: McDonald's is launching a massive Home Alone collaboration for the holiday season, and Macaulay Culkin has reprised his role as Kevin to celebrate.
articles.body:
McDonald's is launching a massive Home Alone collaboration for the holiday season.

The promotion, available across U.S. locations on December 1, comes with Home Alone variants for some of the fast-food chain's most popular meals. We’re talking Quarter Pounders, Nuggets, and, of course, the Big Mac.

Each meal comes with one pair of collectible socks, with four total pairs available across the promotion. The limited-time offer also introduces several new pizza-flavored McDonald’s menu items inspired by Kevin’s hijinks.

Macaulay Culkin reprised his role as the mischievous Kevin to promote the collaboration. A new commercial features grown-up Kevin having a blast in an emptied out McDonald’s restaurant — and showing off his new socks.

"What I love about this collaboration is that the 'Home Alone Meal' captures something bigger than just one character," said Culkin in a statement. "It's about the playful spirit that resonates with people across generations."

To achieve that playful spirit, the Home Alone Meal swaps regular McDonald's fries for the new Pizza McShaker flavor, which comes with a Little Nero’s seasoning packet. Otherwise, most of the meals are pretty similar to the standard versions, just with some socks thrown in.

The four pairs of collectible socks each feature a specific character: Kevin himself, and some McDonald's classics — Grimace, the Hamburglar, and Birdie the Early Bird. They’re pretty much your standard holiday socks, detailed with the classic Golden Arches logo and a small image of the McCallister's house.

Two new standalone items will also be available for a limited time: the Mini Pizza Sharebox and the Everything Sundae McFlurry. The Little Nero's pizza box comes with four crispy cheese and tomato pizza pies, while the McFlurry is packed with Oreos, crushed Smarties, and a chocolate sauce. The pizza obviously references Kevin’s big order in Home Alone, while the McFlurry references Kevin’s gargantuan sundae in Home Alone 2. Yep, we’re getting into sequel territory.

Of course, this wouldn’t be a real fast-food collab without a funky new sauce. The pizza theme continues with 'Lovely Cheese Pizza Dipping Sauce,' a creamy blend of parmesan cheese, tomato flavor, and garden herbs.

The Home Alone Meal launches on December 1 for as long as supplies last. Disney+ trials are being added to McDonald’s Rewards for in-app purchases, giving you a chance to watch the movie while you enjoy your pizza fries. McDonald’s is also currently offering the Pokémon Happy Meal , which will likely run concurrently with the Home Alone collab.

articles.title: Jensen Huang Says He Would Return to Nvidia if Its Board of Directors Ask Him To
articles.summary: Former Nvidia boss Jensen Huang has said he is ready to return to the company he co-founded, after he resigned amid a scandal involving infidelity and alleged espionage.
articles.body:
Former Nvidia boss Jensen Huang has said he is ready to return to the company he co-founded, after he resigned amid a scandal involving infidelity and alleged espionage.

In a social media post , Huang issued a statement apologizing for the problems he'd caused both Nvidia and his family, and insisted he would be willing to return as CEO if Nvidia's Board of Directors decided it was in the best interest in the company.

Huang's statement comes after it was reported that he will appear before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China Select Committees on December 1. "The American people need answers on Mr. Huang and Nvidia’s role in allowing dangerous PRC actors to access our most advanced chips, as well as the role of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in this scandal,” Reps. Brian Mast, R-Fla., John Moolenaar, R-Mich., and Rick Crawford, R-Ark., the chairs of the Foreign Affairs, China Select and Intelligence Committees, said in a statement reported by CNBC .

The former CEO was reportedly exploring returning to Nvidia over the weekend , as Nvidia employees and other tech CEOs rallied to his defense. Despite Huang's willingness to step back onto Nvidia's throne, at least one member of the Board has already come out and told CNBC that it was uninterested in bringing him back, and the company just implemented a new oversight committee in the aftermath of the scandal.

It's still not clear what the future holds for Nvidia as this scandal continues to develop. Whether Huang returns or not will likely depend on what Nvidia's internal investigation turns up. No matter what, the fallout from this chapter in Nvidia's history probably doesn't bode well for the gaming hardware that got the company started 33 years ago .

articles.title: Magnetic Press Brings French Sci-Fi Classic TER to American Shores for the First Time
articles.summary: TER is a modern classic of the French comic book scene, and it's finally getting an English language translation courtesy of Magnetic Press.
articles.body:
The sci-fi graphic novel TER is widely regarded as a modern classic of the French comics scene, and it's finally being translated to English courtesy of Magnetic Press. As the book hits Kickstarter, IGN can exclusively debut a new preview of TER.

Check out the slideshow gallery below for an exclusive look at TER:

TER is written by Rudolphe (Trent) and illustrated by Christophe Dubois (La ballade de Magdalena). This new hardcover edition collects the entire story in one volume. Here's the official description for TER:

In the world of TER, people live a rustic life, like medieval villagers among the ruins of machine-like relics that they treat as religious artifacts because no one remembers their true purpose. When young tomb‑raider Pip cracks open an ancient grave, he finds a naked, mute stranger inside, marked with a strange tattoo and an instinctive ability to repair these ancient devices that no one understands. The villagers call him Mandor, and as he learns to speak and rebuild this forgotten technology, whispers start to spread: is he a savior, a prophet, or something far more dangerous?

Mandor’s quest to uncover his own identity leads him across deserts, derelict structures, and buried secrets until he discovers a truth that shatters everything – Ter isn’t a planet at all, but a colossal, decaying generation ship whose inhabitants have forgotten their ancient origins. What begins as a mystery unfolds into a grand, atmospheric space opera that blends isolation, identity, myth, and the rediscovery of a lost-yet-futuristic civilization.

“TER’s setting is unlike typical sci‑fi in that villagers live in a pseudo‑medieval society built atop ancient technology they no longer understand. It’s Nausicaä meets LOST inside a derelict generation ship,” said Magnetic Press’ Director of Publishing, Mike Kennedy, in a statement. “This fusion of undeveloped life and forgotten futurism creates a haunting, immersive atmosphere, guiding the reader to discover these futuristic wonders along with the unwary villagers.”

articles.title: Kevin Smith Explains How Marvel and Star Wars Collide in Hope Assembles Crossover
articles.summary: We chat with writer Kevin Smith about the unlikeliest crossover ever, as two pop culture juggernauts collide in Star Wars/Marvel: Hope Assembles.
articles.body:
Marvel Comics is kicking off 2027 with one of the most unexpected projects we've ever seen from the publisher. Star Wars/Marvel: Hope Assembles brings these two iconic universes together at long last, as the classic cast of Star Wars: A New Hope suddenly appears in the present-day Marvel Universe. The whole thing is overseen by two creators with plenty of nerdy bona fides: writer Kevin Smith (Clerks) and artist David Marquez (Miles Morales: Ultimate Spider-Man).

IGN recently had a chance to chat briefly with Smith to find out more about how this massive crossover came to be and which team-ups he's most enjoying. Read on to learn more.

Star Wars/Marvel: Hope Assembles #1 Preview Gallery

As you might expect, Smith was as taken aback as anyone when he was first approached by Marvel to pitch for the series. It took a bit of thinking and soul-searching before he arrived at what he felt was the right approach for this story.

"I was honored but hesitant," Smith tells IGN. "Playing with someone else’s toys, you run the risk of upsetting folks who hold these characters near and dear — so I gave it a second before I said yes, weighing the possible pros and cons. Ultimately, I thought of the young version of me, who’d be flabbergasted that I was even thinking of not saying yes. That kid had subscriptions to Star Wars, Spider-Man, and Vision and the Scarlet Witch, and dreamed they’d all crossover one day."

Smith continues, "After 50 years, that day had finally come — and if I were to pass it up for any reason, the young me wouldn’t even recognize the senior version of him, let alone understand any reason he’d give for passing on the ultimate story of hope… out of fear. I pitched Marvel and Lucasfilm how I thought the story could play out, and surprisingly, they liked my take. It’s been the most fun writing gig I’ve ever had."

Smith explains that there were some ground rules established from the start. It was Marvel and Lucasfilm's mandate that the story treat the Marvel Universe as the "real world" and that the Star Wars characters would appear straight out of the movie.

"There were ground rules I was given at the start: the Marvel characters were 'real' and — just like in our reality — Star Wars is a movie they’ve all seen (except Cap)," Smith says. "As a mandate, I didn’t bump into that at all — because, as a fan, that made sense to me."

However, Smith did have one important suggestion — that the series limit itself strictly to the cast of A New Hope rather than attempt to draw in the whole of the Skywalker Saga.

"Originally, it was going to be characters from the ENTIRE Star Wars saga," Smith reveals. "But since we’re celebrating the 50th anniversary of Star Wars specifically, I suggested we focus solely on A New Hope."

As you might expect, one of the real joys of a book like this is finding ways to play the characters of both franchises off of one another. We asked Smith which team-ups he's most enjoyed writing, and he had several top of mind.

"Even though I’ve seen Star Wars over a hundred times, I still sat down and watched it again, this time taking notes about plot points and memorable moments I wanted to shout out. Then when I was writing the scripts, I looked for sensible and unlikely team-ups that I’d wanna see as a fan," Smith says. "Spider-Man’s storyline with Luke is something I leaned into because both characters are the ultimate avatars of hope. And I loved pitting Tony Stark against Princess Leia because it was like swapping Han for Iron Man. And writing for Vader and Doom was as satisfying as watching the Death Star blow up."

Star Wars/Marvel: Hope Assembles #1 will be released on January 13, 2027. You can preorder a copy at your local comic shop .

articles.title: 3 Things to Help You Get Started in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake
articles.body:
We’re back with a new episode of our The Long Game series, where we share things you can invest in early in games that pay off in the long run. This time, we’re taking a nostalgic trip back to Hyrule for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake.

Previous installments in this series have focused on important skills or items you can unlock early, but those kinds of things don’t really apply this time around. Most of your gear and tools are given to you at set points in your adventure, so I’m not going to ruin the sense of discovery by going into detail about those.

Instead, this article will provide a few pieces of advice you can implement as soon as the game begins. So if you’re experiencing the joy of Ocarina of Time for the first time or are revisiting it after a couple decades and don’t remember the finer points, these are designed to help you get into the spirit of the game quickly.

A lot of the characters in Ocarina of Time have useful information or side quests to give you, and they won’t be marked with exclamation points over their heads or question marks on the map. You’ll need to walk up to them and talk to them on your own.

Sometimes, it’ll be obvious what they want and how you can help them. Other times, you’ll need to combine pieces of information given by multiple characters to figure out what they’re hinting at. It’s a game that rewards you for paying attention and taking the initiative of trying things it doesn’t directly spell out for you.

You can utilize this advice as soon as the game begins. You start in Kokiri Forest, but if all you do is hyper focus on getting to the Great Deku Tree, you’ll miss chances to get to know your fellow Kokiri and make some Rupees while you’re at it. So it pays to take your time.

That applies to exploration too. There are areas of Hyrule that the story either won’t require you to go into at all or that you won’t have to set foot in for a long time, but there are rewards if you do so on your own earlier. So don’t be afraid to venture off the beaten path to see what you can find.

Occasionally, you’ll find your path blocked by something that you don’t have a way to deal with right now. I would advise making note of that and coming back after you’ve found some more tools. And here’s one specific tip that might come in handy: If you see the Triforce etched on the ground or wall, you might want to play something on your ocarina…

Keep an Eye and Ear Out for Gold Skulltulas

The early game will introduce you to Gold Skulltulas, the biggest collectable hunt in Ocarina of Time. They glow with a golden light and make a kind of skittering or scratching noise that you can hear when you get close to them. Some of them are very well hidden, so if you hear their trademark noise, stop and look around.

They might be hiding around a corner, behind a destructible wall, or in any number of other places. They tend to like dark places, so you’ll find a lot of them in dungeons or at night. If it’s daytime and you see a spider web, that’s marking a spot where a Gold Skulltula will appear at night. So if you have a way to immediately turn things to night, you should do that.

Once you kill a Gold Skulltula, they’ll leave behind a token you need to collect. Some will be in areas you can’t physically reach, so you’ll need a specific tool capable of retrieving things from a distance. For every 10 Gold Skulltula tokens you collect, you can trade them for rewards at a house in Kakariko Village. Two of these rewards increase the size of your wallet, allowing you to carry more Rupees at a time. These wallet upgrades are required if you want to unlock all the Great Fairies, so it’s a good idea to do some Gold Skulltula hunting early on.

There are several minigames sprinkled across Ocarina of Time, and they’re generally short, sweet, and give good rewards. You’ll find multiple shooting gallery–style games that will allow you to upgrade your carrying capacity for whatever tool you used to win the games.

Other minigames range from fishing to foot races to diving challenges, and you’ll get Pieces of Heart for many of them. Some of these minigames will be in obvious places, like buildings marked with huge signs. Others will require talking to certain characters who will challenge you, which brings things full circle and once again encourages you to talk to everyone. You never know what rewards await.

articles.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Features Joseph Zada as Young Haymitch Abernathy and Gives the Series Full-Circle Closure
articles.summary: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping review: Haymitch Abernathy’s backstory is revealed in this Hunger Games prequel.
articles.body:
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters on November 20.

The last 14 years have featured a lot of big screen Reapings as YA novelist Suzanne Collins’ dystopian The Hunger Games books have been adapted into six individual films. A franchise based on children murdering one another doesn’t exactly scream “blockbuster hit,” but Collins’ reluctant heroine Katniss Everdeen (as embodied by Jennifer Lawrence) captured the hearts and minds of Millennial readers and moviegoers, and so the franchise goes on.

Under the uninterrupted guidance of producer Nina Jacobson and executive producer/director Francis Lawrence, Collins’ surprise standalone prequel books, The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes and Sunrise on the Reaping, have also been adapted into big budget movies. The former revealed Coriolanus Snow’s (Tom Blyth) origin story before he turned into a white-haired, totalitarian child killer (Donald Sutherland), while the latter and latest explains the cascading tragedies that created Panem’s lore around Second Quarter Quell victor Haymitch Abernathy, and ultimately why he mentored Katniss and Peeta (Josh Hutcherson) the way he did after their Reaping 24 years later.

While Woody Harrelson brought the perennially sauced Haymitch to vivid life in the first four Hunger Games films, the details about what prompted the character to retreat into booze and solitude primarily remained a mystery. That alone is a decent reason to add another chapter to the franchise — fleshing out the beloved character and giving him his due — but there’s also an equally strong case against fetishizing (again) the bleak and relentlessly punitive Capitol practice of wiping out 24 to 48 children in spectacular fashion. Thankfully, Jacobson and Lawrence cast the hell out of this chapter by featuring an incredible ensemble of generational actors, and most importantly entrusting the emotional heart of the film to Aussie actor Joseph Zada in his star-making performance as young Haymitch.

And though Sunrise sticks to the franchise’s familiar structure of Reaping, tribute training, arena survival, and outcome, screenwriters Billy Ray and Michael Lesslie wisely refashion the details in bold and unexpected ways, resulting in maximum emotional and political impact for a franchise that needs a fresh perspective so it doesn’t devolve into the bread and circuses Collins so astutely satirizes in her books.

Set 24 years before the events of The Hunger Games, this story begins on the 16th birthday of District 12’s affable teen Haymitch Abernathy (​​Joseph Zada). Unfortunately, his day of celebration coincides with the annual Reaping ceremony where Capitol representatives arrive to enforce and broadcast a mandatory lottery that will doom one boy and one girl to compete in the vindictive Hunger Games. Because this year is a Quarter Quell celebration, four children are Reaped, and Haymitch earns his way onto the “team” after he protects his Covey girlfriend, Lenore Dove Baird (Whitney Peak), from speaking out against the Capitol.

As the pack of tributes/neighbors are shuttled to the Capitol, we get to know prickly Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace), nervous oddsmaker Wyatt Callow (Ben Wang), and little Louella McCoy (Molly McCann) as they sweat what lays ahead of them. With his Harrelson-esque twang and laconic countenance, Zada charms his 12 brethren by displaying Haymitch’s inherent empathy and kindness like a superpower. He’s able to calm those around him while growing increasingly incensed about the callous treatment foisted upon them. What Sunrise does best is purposefully remix the familiar tropes of the Games — mentor lessons, getting styled for camera, training for the arena — into a simmering thriller that connects the disenfranchised victors of the Games with secret sympathizers who are tired of Snow’s tyrannical grip on Panem.

Exposing the rot at the core of Snow’s regime distinguishes Sunrise from other chapters; this time around, Lawrence is surprisingly ruthless in portraying the Capitol’s enablers and sycophants. There’s no sentimentality extended to ghoulishly violent District 12 escort Drusilla Sickle (in a demented performance by Glenn Close) and her lavender marriage to stylist husband Magno Stift (Billy Porter). Even Elle Fanning’s capricious take on young Effie Trinket and Kieran Culkin’s coldly chaotic approach to Master of Ceremonies Caesar Flickerman are framed in a harsher light than Elizabeth Banks’ Effie or Stanley Tucci’s Caesar, and the film is better for it. Not even future rebellion architect and current Games producer Plutarch Heavensbee’s (Jesse Plemons) gets a pass for his sins of collusion, drawing a much stronger line in the sand about the evil Ralph Fiennes’ middle-aged Snow intentionally sows, and how complicit the Capitol residents are with their rapturous participation.

Visually, there’s much to admire about Uli Hanisch’s production design of the Quarter Quell arena and how beautifully cinematographer Jo Willems captures it. It’s like Ari Aster’s Midsommar had a baby with a Disney princess movie; the twisted landscape is a minefield of razor butterflies, rabid squirrels, and kamikaze birds for the tributes to survive. And much like Catching Fire, the arena isn’t just a backdrop but a puzzle to be solved as Haymitch embarks on a personal mission to cut the head off Snow’s showpiece.

Unlike The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes, Sunrise is also long but paced more evenly, staying focused on Haymitch’s arc of defiance and then the heavy price he’s made to pay that eventually breaks him. Zada’s performance is so vulnerable and compelling that it ranks up there with Lawrence’s Katniss and Sutherland’s Snow in terms of indelible characterizations. Plemons is also terrific in portraying a more openly passionate Heavensbee who hasn’t yet learned to disappear from Snow’s eyeline.

In keeping with the hope that permeates Collins’ books and these films, Lawrence wraps up Sunrise by connecting it to the epilogue of Mockingjay – Part 2, and in doing so creates the rare full-circle cinematic moment that’s satisfying and appropriately feels like earned closure. Hopefully, the team (including Collins) sees it that way too, and they end the franchise here on a high note.

Across the arc of these six films, Collins, Jacobson, and Lawrence have successfully personalized the murky concept of authoritarianism, effectively warning younger generations how quickly ​​fascism can creep out of the pages of history and speculative science fiction into real life. And though The Hunger Games franchise is guilty of being too maximalist at times, there’s no denying the impact it’s had on popular culture — not only in memes, but in telling a satisfying allegory about the heartbreaking cost of war.

articles.title: 'These Decisions Are Never Easy' — Civilization Developer Firaxis Lays Off One Third of Its Workforce
articles.summary: Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis Games is laying off around 60 people, which amounts to approximately one third of its workforce, according to a Bloomberg report. The studio head of the Maryland-based development studio is also departing.
articles.body:
Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis Games is laying off around 60 people, which amounts to approximately one third of its workforce, according to a Bloomberg report. The studio head of the Maryland-based development studio is also departing.

2K, the publishing arm that handles Firaxis, BioShock games, the Mafia series, and various sports titles under Take-Two, gave Bloomberg a comment on the layoffs.

“Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength — designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years,” said a 2K spokesperson.

“As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.”

The 4X strategy game series has been one of the quiet giants under the 2K label, but the most recent entry, Civilization 7, divided players. Reviews for the game on Steam are mixed, with players complaining about radical structural changes to long-standing franchise traditions, a lack of polish, and predatory implementation of monetization.

According to the report, Firaxis is also working on a new game in its turn-based alien invasion series, XCOM. However, the team has been facing development struggles and recently missed a key development milestone.

Bloomberg’s anonymous sources claim that development of the new XCOM will continue, but will likely face some kind of shakeup following the cuts to staffing.

Firaxis also laid off an unannounced number of developers last year , following the launch of Civilization 7, despite 2K claiming sales of the game were “consistent with expectations.”

The studio’s previous major launch, Marvel’s Midnight Suns, performed poorly . At the time, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick told Bloomberg that "it's possible the release window wasn't perfect" but that he thinks it could keep selling over a long period of time.
